# 08 - Lithium-Sulfur Batteries

Acquisition method: Web research note synthesized from public sources.

- Stellantis and Zeta lithium-sulfur agreement: https://www.stellantis.com/en/news/press-releases/2024/december/stellantis-and-zeta-energy-announce-agreement-to-develop-lithium-sulfur-ev-batteries

## What It Is

Lithium-sulfur batteries use sulfur-based cathodes and lithium-based anodes. Sulfur is abundant and inexpensive, and the chemistry can avoid nickel, cobalt, manganese, and graphite.

## Automotive Relevance Today

Lithium-sulfur is not a mainstream EV battery today, but it has real automotive partnerships. Stellantis invested in Lyten in 2023 and announced a joint development agreement with Zeta Energy in 2024. Chrysler's Halcyon concept uses an 800 V lithium-sulfur battery concept.

## Strengths

The appeal is high theoretical gravimetric energy density and lower material cost. Stellantis says lithium-sulfur has potential to deliver more than twice the energy density of lithium-ion, while avoiding nickel, cobalt, and manganese in the cathode. Zeta and Stellantis target a lighter pack with the same usable energy, up to 50% faster charging, and cost less than half current lithium-ion on a per-kWh basis.

Lithium-sulfur could also improve supply-chain sovereignty because sulfur is widely available and can come from industrial byproducts.

## Weaknesses

The major challenges are cycle life, polysulfide shuttle, lithium-metal stability, swelling, self-discharge, and volumetric energy density. High gravimetric energy density does not automatically mean a compact EV pack. Automotive warranties require thousands of real-world cycles, calendar-life stability, and broad temperature tolerance.

Lyten uses 3D graphene to address polysulfide shuttle challenges; Zeta describes proprietary anode and cathode technology. These claims still require broad public automotive validation.

## Future Development

Likely development path:

- Specialty, aerospace, defense, and non-EV cells first.
- Concept vehicles and validation fleets.
- Automotive production planning toward 2030 if cycle life and manufacturing targets are met.

Stellantis and Zeta explicitly target use in Stellantis electric vehicles by 2030 if development succeeds.

## Commercialization Outlook

Lithium-sulfur is a credible future option but higher-risk than silicon-enhanced lithium-ion or LMR. It could be disruptive if it reaches automotive cycle life and volumetric density targets, but it should be treated as a hypothesis rather than a near-term baseline.

## Implications for Older EV Value

If lithium-sulfur reaches market around 2030 with much lower cost and lighter packs, it could sharply affect expectations for older long-range EVs. Until production vehicles exist, the current residual-value impact should be limited.
